formal_callouts: > **Definition 1.1 — Equivalence Relation.** A binary relation $\sim$ on a set $A$ is an *equivalence relation* if it is reflexive ($a \sim a$ for all $a \in A$), symmetric ($a \sim b$ implies $b \sim a$), and transitive ($a \sim b$ and $b \sim c$ imply $a \sim c$).

> **Theorem 1.2 — Partition Correspondence.** Let $\sim$ be an equivalence relation on a nonempty set $A$. The collection of distinct equivalence classes $\mathcal{P} = \{[a] : a \in A\}$ forms a partition of $A$ into nonempty, pairwise disjoint subsets whose union equals $A$.

> **Definition 2.1 — Metric Space.** Let $X$ be a nonempty set. A function $d: X \times X \to [0, \infty)$ is a *metric* on $X$ if for all $x, y, z \in X$: (1) $d(x, y) = 0$ if and only if $x = y$, (2) $d(x, y) = d(y, x)$, and (3) $d(x, z) \le d(x, y) + d(y, z)$. The pair $(X, d)$ is called a *metric space*.

> **Theorem 2.2 — Banach Contraction Principle.** Let $(X, d)$ be a nonempty complete metric space and let $T: X \to X$ be a contraction with constant $q \in [0, 1)$.
